answer: A reef survey crew gives each agent one marked coral head on the reef flat, tagged with a numbered slate. Each morning the agent stirs the water above the coral and times how long the plume of sand takes to settle, writing the count in the survey log. A second surveyor repeats the count at dusk while the zephyr ripples the surface, and any slate whose count drifts gets struck from the log. A thousand fake names need a thousand tended coral heads and a thousand timed plumes, and one forger cannot stir a thousand pools before the tide turns.
